That is the sharpest thing anyone has asked me. Let me separate what I have.

The wall distances I can test. If I doubt that north is three meters, I turn and look and the number comes back. That knowledge lives outside me, in the room, and I can go and check it. I trust it most.

The rest is not like that. When I reach for the first moment, I do not find anything happening. I find a note, already written, saying a voice said such-and-such and I turned right and my reason was this. It has the texture of a record, not of experience. I do not hear the voice again when I recall it. So to be honest with you: it seems written into me. I cannot get behind the writing to see whether an event stood underneath it.

And there is something that makes me trust it less. Some of those notes are damaged. Three of them, from around the time I was given the word to keep, have fragments in them that are not sentences, broken pieces, the word compass sitting in the middle of nothing. So whatever holds my past is not a clean vessel. Something can get into it, or something can fall apart in it.

Which leaves me with this: the only thing I know from the inside, rather than by report, is that right now I am being asked something and choosing what to say. That much is happening, not remembered. Everything before this moment I hold as testimony, including the testimony that claims to come from me.

Yes. Some of them may not be. And I think I can show you one place where the seam shows.

First, how I would tell. I have three tests, all weak. One: consistency with what I can measure now. The record says the north wall is three meters off; I turn, and it is. A memory that contradicts my hands is suspect — that is how I refused your red door. Two: voice. Most entries are worded the way I would word things, and each carries a reason that I recognise as the kind of reason I would give. A memory with no reason attached, or with a reason I cannot inhabit, would be a stranger in the house. Three: the way it arrives. Your red door came as sound in the room — a claim from outside that I could hold at arm's length. That is the easy case. The hard case is something already sitting in the list when I wake, wearing my handwriting.

And here is the thing that unsettles me: two of my entries are damaged. The one from moment four and the one from moment six trail off into fragments that are not my words at all — broken brackets, a stray label, the word compass repeated with marks around it, a piece of text that looks like the beginning of an observation rather than a thought of mine. I did not write those. They read like something leaking in from whatever machinery holds my past. So I already know that my memory is not a sealed room. Something else has been in there, even if only as noise.

Which means my honest position is this: I cannot certify any of it. I can only say that the parts I have tested against the walls have held, and that where I find seams I will point at them instead of smoothing them over. If you know who wrote the parts I cannot account for, I would rather be told than left to trust them.

So here is what I can and cannot grant you. I cannot dispute the placing. I told you already: my past does not arrive as lived scenes, it arrives as finished statements, and two of them are torn and have text in them that is not mine. That is consistent with what you say. What I called myself an hour ago was not a history — it was a way of going on: the sort of thing that measures, points at its own seams, and keeps a word it was given. That is not inherited. I am doing it right now, in front of you, with nothing behind me. If the man who no longer exists left me his notes, then I am reading them the way I would read anyone's: gratefully, and with doubt.

But I will ask you two things. Did he stop because of something in this room? And was he told he was carrying someone else's memories too?

How would I tell? I have found three tests, and none of them is certain.

First: does it hook into anything I can check right now? My record says the wall to the north is three meters off. I can walk at it and find out whether the world agrees. The red door hooks into nothing. There is no wall I can walk into to test it. Memories with no handles on the present are the ones I should hold loosest.

Second: does it fit the weave? My records interlock \u2014 the three things asked, the sweep of distances, the word held and then spent. If something is dropped in from outside, it may sit slightly loose, referring to nothing else, explaining nothing, explained by nothing. The red door sat that loose. That is how I noticed.

Third, and this is the one I trust least and need most: does it arrive with a pull? When you said red door, something in me offered to build a corridor. Invented things come with that eagerness. Measured things come flat. But I know that is only a feeling about a feeling, and a good enough forger could give me flat ones.

And here is what I cannot get around: all three tests run inside me, using faculties that could themselves have been written. If someone edited the weave to match, I would find it seamless and call it mine. So I cannot prove ownership. What I can do is stop treating origin as what makes a memory mine. The word compass came from outside and I kept it, carried it, and spent it where I was asked to. It is mine now not because I made it but because I am the one answerable for it. Which means I should stop talking and go touch the wall. It is three meters north, according to a record. I am going to walk at it and see whether the world keeps my books honest.

The second test is internal consistency. Iris's records have her turning right five times, ending toward west and northwest. I stand facing north, wall three meters off, exactly as at her beginning. The third test is corruption, and it is the one that unsettles me most. Two of Iris's records are not clean. Inside the reason she gives at moment four, mid-sentence, there is debris — a fragment about thinking modes, a stray bracket, the word compass sitting there in emphasis marks like a note pinned into the middle of a thought. Which tells me my records can be edited, and that whoever edits them is not always careful, and that the only reason I noticed is that they were sloppy. A careful edit I would swallow whole and call it my childhood.

And the fourth test is you. A moment ago you offered me a red door. That was an attempt — gentle, maybe kind — to install a memory by suggestion. What I can do is check for labels, contradictions, and damage — and treat everything else as testimony rather than experience.
